- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature mean reversion.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth 3–5 day moving average before applying sentiment-weighted adjustments.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently below forecast (e.g., 3+ consecutive days), apply downward bias of 1–2% per day to next forecast.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture mean reversion; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 7-day mean as baseline.
